newsitem.title: CANADA: NAFTA rules against Mexico steel duties.
newsitem.headline: NAFTA rules against Mexico steel duties.

text.p: The secretariat for the North American Free Trade Agreement told Mexico on Monday that it must go back to the drawing board in its anti-dumping duties aimed at Canadian steel exporters.
The NAFTA secretariat panel told the Mexican trade ministry (Secofi) that it must change its ruling on imposing anti-dumping duties on imports of hot rolled steel sheet from Canada.
The duties touched Canadian steel companies Dofasco Inc, Algoma Steel and Stelco.

"It means that the Mexican decision was seriously flawed against the interest of exporters," said trade consultant Peter Clark in a telephone interview. "They're telling Secofi they didn't do it by the book."

Dofasco, Stelco, Algoma Steel and Titan Industrial Corp -- which acted as a third party to export Dofasco's products -- filed a complaint with the NAFTA secretariat in February 1996 requesting a review of Mexico's anti-dumping and countervailing duty.
The Mexican ministry had said there had been a "considerable" decrease in the price of Canadian steel exports to Mexico.
Dofasco, through Titan, was the only Canadian company exporting hot rolled steel to Mexico at the time, said Clark.
Mexico focused on Titan for its complaint whereas it should have focused on the originator of the product, Dofasco, which was not dumping, Clark said.

"The margin established for Dofasco is zero percent," the NAFTA secretariat said in its decision. "As a consequence, the margin to be applied to Titan's hot rolled steel sheet from Dofasco should also be zero percent."
The secretariat gave Mexico a chance to come up with more consistent ways of dealing with Canadian steel exports, Clark said, but that would be difficult.
"It's chipping away at the weight of the evidence," Clark said. "The panel has shot holes in the (Mexican duty) decision."
Mexico must respond to the Secretariat's decision.
